title: Projection compatibility of the second graph constituent
statement: Let A be a finite commutative ring, f:X→Y a morphism of arbitrary schemes, c a supplied open/proper compactification and t=(a,e,p) a proper/open/proper presentation of f. Form the concrete graph presentations t1,t2 and comparison factors B1,B2,D of [def-sf-graph-projection-stages]. For every M in D(X_et,A) and K in D(Y_et,A), tensor B2_M with K and then apply the successive word projection of the second graph presentation t2. The result equals the original word projection for t followed by B2 evaluated at M tensor Lf*K. These are the exact sfGraphWordProjection coefficient compositors [def-sf-etale-graph-word-projection]. No other graph constituent is used in this assertion, and no qc, Noetherianity or boundedness is required.

proof.text: Write s for the second proper graph, q for its projection to U, b for the supporting open, and r for the projection to P. Then s followed by q equals a. The specified second-side comparison is Rp(Je(alpha inverse)), followed by Rp(gamma), followed by beta, where alpha is the proper compositor for s,q, gamma is the Cartesian proper/open exchange, and beta is the proper compositor for r,p. Expand only these functor associators and whiskerings.

Use the already proved properStrength_comp constituent of the compactification-tower calculation at s,q and at r,p, and its mixed_twisted_projection constituent for q,b,e,r. An elementary categorical pasting lemma cancels only alpha, moves the inner strength through the exchange by naturality, applies the mixed square, and then moves the resulting coefficient change through beta. This gives the projection square at the raw coefficient Ls Lq Le Lp K. No projection arrow is inverted.

Identify the final coefficient path by three component associativity identities for derived pullback composition, applied to (sb,r,p), (s,b,r), and (s,q,e). Naturality of the s,b compositor moves the r,p coefficient map. Expand the square pullback comparison and cancel its inverse compositor. The resulting path is exactly the canonical sfGraphWordProjection coefficient for the second presentation.

Postcompose the raw square with tensor of the inverse s,q pullback compositor followed by the original word coefficient. Naturality of the second-side isomorphism moves this map across the comparison. Coefficient naturality of open and proper projection gives the second word projection; cancellation of the s,q compositor gives the original word projection. Thus the displayed equation has precisely the specified endpoint coefficients. Normalize the endpoint by explicitly unfolding sfGraphWordProjection and its imported sfGraphProjectionWord definition, distributing the final coefficient composite through the tensor, proper image and open extension functors.
